title: Prove the (0,2,1,1) three-frame profile admits no seven-call word.
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped character proof. No new κ and no word.

In the PR2085/2112 formal register model, the seven-call profile `(a,b,p,q,r,s,t) = (0,2,1,1,1,1,1)` admits no word. The determinant equation is `R+S+T = 3A+B = diag(3,1)`. Every decomposition into three nonzero symmetric rational rank-one matrices admits an AB or PQ character that detects two calls and four targets. The selected record stays κ = `781451/250000000`.

This is a proof for this one named census profile. It is not a multiplication theorem, not an exhaustive census of the other profiles, and not a heuristic search. The other nineteen three-frame census profiles, and every decomposition with four or more added frames, remain open. The settled all-old-once profile `(1,1,1,1)/(1,1,1)` is not redone.

## Task and overlap

Session r123. The assigned question is one other named profile from the seven-call census in discussion comment 19377345, not the settled profile `(1,1,1,1)/(1,1,1)`, and not the four-frame remainder.

Profile taken: old counts `(0,2,1,1)` with added multiplicities `(1,1,1)`. That tuple is one of the twelve profiles the census lists with 24 positive-dimensional spaces.

Base commit: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` (upstream CrocSwap main, re-fetched 2026-11-10T02:35:54Z and unchanged). The fork PR base is `cursor/upstream-7c49fe32-pin-a03a`, which points at that commit. Priority revision 8. The priority file still quotes an older selected decimal; the frontier value used here is the selected record.

Task card: `bit-new-register-model`, `scope_status: changed`. The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers one profile left open by the all-old-once exclusion.

Overlap recheck on 2026-11-10: discussion #1166 contains `(0,2,1,1)` only in the census comment 19377345. No later comment settles it. Fork draft PR #155 and branch `cursor/three-signed-old-once-a03a` exclude only `(1,1,1,1)/(1,1,1)`. No other fork branch is named for this profile. Open upstream PR titles did not show another three-signed census profile. GitHub code search was rate-limited, so this is not a claim that every blob was searched.

## Validation

Python 3.12. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/three-signed-b-twice --check-only
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/three-signed-b-twice
python3 scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/three-signed-b-twice --ref HEAD --check-modes
```

Observed: `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with `outcome=completed`, and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` at `ed127d7ab6067daf8a48def1445da5864ad113df`. The direct check is `python3 -I -W error -B research/three-signed-b-twice/verify.py`, also run with `-O`. Both printed `PASS three-signed-b-twice character checks`.

`verify.py` expands the scale-bracket and Cramer-determinant polynomials and checks that each identity is exact. It exhausts the 32 odd residue classes of the mod-8 discriminant lemma, checks the axial and diagonal quadratic valuations, and checks the strict valuation gaps used in the Cramer case. It then checks explicit characters on five declared frames: an integral nonparallel triple, a negative frame, a fractional frame, a parallel opposite-scale pair, and a frame equal to the old matrix `B`. Each witness detects two calls and four targets. Failure controls reject a tampered sum, reject `I` as a rank-one summand, and reject an even-even-even form. The single-line box is a finite corroboration of Lemma 3 on coordinates and denominators at most 12. That box is not the proof; Sections 4 through 6 of `PROOF.md` are.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the selected-result cold replay, `scripts/research_selected_baseline.py`, the full predecessor replay of PR #6190, and the source-history preflight. This checkout is shallow, so `check_research_commit.py --check-source-history` reported that full Git history is required. The pin check in `research_package.py --check-only` did resolve the declared blobs.

## Credit

The register model is Cinna Davis's PR2085/2112 formal model. The determinant and first-order inequality are the PR2910 package as recorded in apoursh's two-signed-frame floor, PR #6190. The census is discussion comment 19377345. The released handoff is comment 19377832. The all-old-once exclusion is unpaidmoon fork PR #155 and is not redone here.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. No independent human or formal-kernel review. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Which of the other nineteen three-frame count profiles survive the same AB/PQ test? A useful first step is the named sibling `(2,0,1,1)/(1,1,1)`, whose residual is `diag(1,3)`. The bilinear form and the constants 3, 6, and 12 here belong to `3A+B` and do not transfer unchanged.

Can four or more added signed rank-one frames lower the eight-call minimum? This three-summand character does not apply. A useful first step is four primitive directions and the shortest determinant equation that uses each new label once.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The census names the profiles as count tuples, while the settled package's `TASK.json` does not list them. Quoting the tuple from comment 19377345, and replying on that handoff rather than opening a second thread, is enough. Linking this once in [discussion #1200](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200) is enough.
